correctness.rationale: The proof rewrites the source's exact positive-part representation in an exact threshold coordinate, uses two direct support inclusions and mass conservation to obtain t G(sigma(t)) -> 1, and then applies elementary asymptotic inversion. Monotonicity of the source multiplier justifies the pointwise derivative asymptotic by difference-quotient squeezing. Homogeneous local scaling yields the similarity profile and support coefficient; symbolic checks confirm all exponent and coefficient identities.

originality.rationale: The source's representation formula, qualitative multiplier convergence, concentration theorem, small-threshold G asymptotics, and limiting weights are prior work and excluded from novelty. The inspected source and nearby papers do not state the full-time localization clock, its explicit dynamic rates, or the local similarity profile. External and repository searches found no source-specific equivalent result; a residual risk remains because the sharpening combines source ingredients with standard asymptotic inversion.

value.rationale: The result converts static signal-sublevel geometry into a quantitative dynamical localization law. It supplies multiplier, peak-height, support-area, and spatial-width exponents with explicit constants and a full local profile; for generic Morse maxima it predicts a t^(-1/4) width and t^(-1/2) support area.
